text: {"frames":["A smell of wet wood and tar drifts down the stairs, and you follow it up to a door that was not there yesterday. Pinned to it is a map of the polders, with a dyke drawn in red ink that nobody in Misty Ford has ever seen. In one corner a tiny windmill has its sails turned the wrong way. Femke tells you the mill only turns when its share is known. What is {x} as a percentage, so the sails can turn the right way?","Bong, the bell rings out of the fog, and it comes from a village that sank under the lake long ago. Thijs runs past with a lantern and says the bell only tolls when the Tower wants an answer. You follow the sound down a staircase that smells of cold cheese and salt. At the bottom a note hangs on the bell rope, saying the bell will ring for each part that is counted. Write {x} as a percentage, so the bell can say how much of the fog is left?","Stay quiet, the watchman is near, Joop whispers at the dyke gate. Nobody has seen him by daylight, only his footprints in the frost at dawn. Tonight a lantern sits on the sill, and its flame leans toward the Tower as if it is listening. A note under it says the gate opens when the watchman's share of the night is known. How do you write {x} as a percentage to open the gate?","You push open the door of the crooked house with the hoist beam, and every window is glowing. Inside, the kettle is warm and the cheese on the table is still soft, but no one is home. Anke's clogs stand by the hearth, and a chalk mark on the wall keeps count in tally lines. The lamps hum a low tune, as if they were waiting for you. Write {x} as a percentage, so the lamps know how much of the house is lit?","Please, help us, the clock keeper calls down the stairs, his voice shaking. The tower clock has just struck an hour that does not exist, and its hands have stopped. Bas holds the key to the clock face and says the hands will move only when the right share is found. A slip of paper lies in the works with a fraction on it and the words write it as a percentage. What is {x} as a percentage, so the clock can strike again?"]}
